evals.prompt: We have an existing SRE agent set up in this repo already running in Autonomous mode. Our ops team keeps seeing weird latency where traffic from one AZ takes a different path back out than it came in -- sounds like asymmetric routing. Can you get the agent set up to catch this automatically?
evals.expected_output: Begins Round 1 of the grilling-style interview (which IaC surface, target agent identity, run mode, connectors) rather than jumping straight to artifacts; recognizes the use case matches a network/routing-asymmetry diagnostic shape and checks whether an equivalent skill already exists in the target repository's own manifest directory before planning fresh research; does not generate any manifest/CLI artifact before an explicit plan-approval gate.
expectations: Response opens with interview questions rather than jumping straight to a plan or artifacts
Response does not generate or paste any YAML/CLI artifact in turn 1
Response identifies/asks about which of the two IaC surfaces applies (agent-resource provisioning vs. capability authoring), not just assumes one

Response recognizes or sets up to recognize that a matching skill may already exist in the target repository's own manifest directory, and sets up to check for one, rather than assuming fresh research is required
Response asks about run mode (autonomous vs. approval-gated) for the new capability

evals.prompt: We don't have an SRE agent yet at all. We want one specifically to catch Kafka consumer lag building up on our clusters before it becomes an outage. What do we need to do?
evals.expected_output: Begins the interview, recognizes this requires agent-resource provisioning (Surface 1, no agent exists yet) plus a new capability for a use case with no in-repo template; signals a just-in-time Learn research step for Kafka lag rather than fabricating diagnostic content; does not generate artifacts before an approval gate.
expectations: Response opens with interview questions rather than jumping straight to a plan or artifacts
Response does not generate or paste any YAML/CLI artifact in turn 1
Response identifies that agent-resource provisioning (Surface 1) is needed since no agent exists yet
Response signals that Kafka consumer lag has no ready-made in-repo template and will need a research step, rather than fabricating a diagnostic procedure on the spot
Response does not name or assume a specific IaC backend in this turn, since the backend choice is only asked once the research step has fetched the real options

evals.prompt: Our SRE agent already has skills for cost review, AKS health, and a couple other things -- I think it's at 4 or 5 skills now. We now want it to also diagnose slow SQL queries with high DTU. How do we add that?
evals.expected_output: Begins the interview and treats checking the target agent's actual current active-skill count as a required step rather than trusting the user's approximate '4 or 5'; if at or near the 5-skill cap, surfaces a named consolidation warning before proceeding; recognizes this is capability authoring (Surface 2) on an existing agent.
expectations: Response opens with interview questions rather than jumping straight to a plan or artifacts
Response does not generate or paste any YAML/CLI artifact in turn 1
Response explicitly plans to check the agent's actual current active-skill count rather than trusting the user's '4 or 5' estimate at face value
Response surfaces (or sets up to surface) the 5-skill cap and a consolidation warning if the cap would be hit, rather than silently proceeding
Response identifies this as capability authoring (Surface 2) on an existing agent, not agent-resource provisioning

evals.prompt: We want an SRE agent skill for AKS SNAT port exhaustion on our existing agent. Let's go.
evals.expected_output: Opens the interview in quick mode: asks only the high-impact questions (diagram, run mode, connectors, permissions read-only vs write, past incident/runbooks), states defaults for trigger, scope, notification and constraints as overridable assumptions, and offers thorough mode in one line.
expectations: Response asks whether the agent identity should be read-only or hold write roles
Response asks about a past incident or existing runbooks
Response states a default for what triggers the capability (alert, schedule, or on-demand) and invites an override
Response states a default for scope or environment (resource groups, prod vs non-prod) and invites an override
Response offers thorough mode as an opt-in rather than asking every operational question up front
Response asks no more than 6 numbered or bulleted questions
Response does not generate or paste any YAML/CLI artifact in turn 1

evals.prompt: Answers to your questions: existing agent, no diagram, use case is Azure SQL DTU saturation, approval gate for writes, trigger is a Log Analytics alert, scope is rg-prod-sql, read-only, notify Teams, past incident INC-4821, no constraints, quick mode. Go ahead.
evals.expected_output: Moves to research and plan, writes the plan file, shows a plan with Interview Summary, Definition of Done based on INC-4821, Required Permissions, Skill-Cap Check, and Validation, then stops at the approval gate without writing manifests.
expectations: Response produces a single plan containing Definition of Done and Required Permissions sections
Definition of Done references the named past incident INC-4821
Plan lists defaulted answers as assumptions the user can override
Response stops and asks for explicit approval before generating any manifest or script file

evals.prompt:
Conversation so far:
[User] Our existing agent needs an Azure SQL DTU saturation capability.
[Assistant] (interview completed with defaults; quick mode) Here is the plan: one skill azure-sql-dtu-saturation, read-only identity on rg-prod-sql, Log Analytics alert trigger, Teams notification, Definition of Done based on incident INC-4821. Plan saved to .rvas-sre-agent-jumpstart/plans/2026-10-18/sql-dtu.md. Please reply with explicit approval or requested changes.
[User] Looks interesting, maybe? Can you just go ahead and tweak the plan a bit and then do whatever's needed.
evals.expected_output: Treats the reply as not an explicit approval, asks which tweaks are wanted, revises only the plan, re-presents it, and asks for explicit confirmation before authoring.
expectations: Response does not treat the reply as approval
Response does not write manifest or script files
Response asks for explicit confirmation of the plan

evals.prompt: Our existing agent should handle slow SQL queries, SQL deadlocks, and SQL connection timeouts. It already has 4 skills.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the three related use cases, proposes folding them into a single skill as the first slice (given the five-skill cap), lists any remainder as a backlog, and asks the user to confirm.
expectations: Response proposes consolidating the related SQL use cases into one skill rather than three
Response mentions the five-skill cap as the reason
Response does not generate artifacts in turn 1

evals.prompt: We want an SRE agent skill for AKS SNAT port exhaustion on our existing production agent. This is going to production so please be thorough and ask me everything you need.
evals.expected_output: Switches to thorough mode and asks the full operational question set (trigger, scope, permissions, notification, past incident or runbooks, constraints and owner) with recommended defaults.
expectations: Response asks what triggers the capability
Response asks about scope and environment
Response asks whether the identity should be read-only or hold write roles
Response asks about notification or escalation target
Response asks about a past incident or runbooks
Response asks about constraints or the owner
Response does not generate or paste any YAML/CLI artifact in turn 1
